librariesLoadFailed: Could not load your libraries — the list below may be out of date.
libraryCreated: Library created — it now shows in the sidebar.
deleteLibraryMessage: Its {count} series stay in your collection (moved to another library) — nothing is deleted from disk.
ovDirect: Direct lookups with your own key or account
ovSetFolder: Set a folder on a library
attnProviderBody: It is turned on as a metadata source, but until its key or sign-in details are entered it is skipped and the built-in service answers.
attnProviderBodyOthers: It is turned on as a metadata source, but until its key or sign-in details are entered it is skipped and the other sources answer.
attnNoSourcesBody: New comics can’t be downloaded until a source is turned on.
attnOneSourceBody: A second source gives searches a fallback when the first misses.
attnNoFolderBody: Downloads fall back to the downloads folder until a library gets one.
attnLibNoFolderBody: Its downloads file into the first library that has one — set a folder to keep them separate.
discardMessage: You edited settings but didn’t save them.
saveFailedUnreachable: Save failed — is the app reachable?
wizardTitle: Walk through the first-run setup again (keys, folders, sources)
ovIntro: How BackIssue is configured at a glance — click a card to jump to its page.
librariesSub: Split the collection into named libraries — each shows as its own entry in the sidebar. A library's type sets how its series behave (manga = chapter-style search, right-to-left reading); its folders are where its comics are filed and scanned. Move series from a volume's … menu.
libraryTypeTitle: Library type — sets how its series behave
matureTitle: Hide this library (and everything in it) from roles without the “View mature content” permission
defaultTitle: New comics for this library are filed here
makeDefaultTitle: Make this the default folder for new comics
libIsDefault: Default library: new comic series go here when you don’t pick one.
libDefaultSet: New comic series now go to {name}
librariesOrder: The arrows set the order libraries appear in the sidebar. The default library is where new comic series go when you don’t pick one.
removeFolderTitle: Remove this folder (files stay on disk)
libFolderPatternTitle: Per-library folder pattern, e.g. {series} for a tree without publisher folders
tagPlacementTitle: Sidecar writes metadata to a .xml next to each archive and never modifies the file — keeps it byte-identical for seeding and share hashing
orgSub: How downloaded comics are named and filed.
renameDownloads: Rename downloaded files to the file pattern (off = keep the source's original filename)
dateNote: {date} is the cover date — November 2011. For the parts on their own: {date:m} 11, {date:y} 2011, {date:mon} Nov. So ({date:m}-{date:y}) gives (11-2011).
patternsNote: Changing these affects new downloads — for existing files use Reorganize library on the Tools page.
maintSub: Fallback locations and how hard the library tools work.
downloadsDirNote: Only used when no library has a folder — normally every download files into its library.
toolWorkersNote: How many files the library tools (convert / verify / tag) process at once — higher overlaps I/O but uses more memory per in-flight file.
dlSub: What happens when you add a series, and how downloads run.
downloadOnAddNote: Adding a series (Library, Discover, Releases, reading lists) immediately queues what its monitoring policy wants. Off = series add empty and you press "Download missing" yourself.
monitorNote: The monitoring policy a series gets when it enters the library — added by hand, from Discover, Releases, reading lists, requests, or an import. All issues keeps the run complete; New issues only wants issues from the newest one onward and leaves the back catalogue alone; Off fetches nothing until you monitor it or pick issues yourself. Any series can be changed later from its … menu.
onlyRequested: Only the issues that were asked for
onlyRequestedNote: When a series is added because of specific issues — an entry on a reading list, a release, a CBL import — it arrives with monitoring off and just those issues wanted, so only they are downloaded (now and if a grab fails later). Adding from the Library or Discover still gets the policy above. Needs "Download on add".
simultaneousNote: How many issues download at once. Higher is faster but more likely to trip a source's rate limits. Applies to the next download.
flaresolverrNote: Some download sites sit behind Cloudflare. FlareSolverr (a small companion service you run — ghcr.io/flaresolverr/flaresolverr) gets past the challenge; point this at its /v1 endpoint. Every source that needs it shares this one setting. Leave blank if none of your sources are behind Cloudflare.
noSourcesWarn: No sources enabled — nothing can download.
usenetDesc: Search Newznab indexers and download via SABnzbd or NZBGet.
managedNote: Managed by an indexer plugin — these manual indexers are ignored while it's enabled.
newznabNote: Newznab (the standard indexer API — e.g. NZBgeek) indexers, searched in order; results are merged.
usenetCompleteNote: Only needed if the client runs on another machine. Map the folder it writes finished downloads to (client's view) onto the path this app reads it at over the network. .cbr releases are converted to .cbz so they can be tagged.
usenetPollingNote: BackIssue hands the NZB to your client under the category you set above (default backissue), watches it, imports each download when it completes (tag + file), and removes it from the client. Downloads are tracked in the database, so an app restart resumes them.
torrentDesc: Search Torznab indexers (Jackett/Prowlarr) and download via qBittorrent, Transmission, or Deluge.
torznabNote: Torznab (the standard indexer API — e.g. Jackett or Prowlarr) feeds, searched in order; results are merged and ranked by seeders.
torrentCompleteNote: Only needed if the download client runs on another machine. Map its content path onto the path this app reads over the network.
torrentPollingNote: BackIssue hands the magnet/.torrent to your client, watches it, and imports each torrent when it completes. After import the torrent is left seeding — manage ratio and removal in the client.
zeroDayAddNew: Add new series I don't follow (confident matches only)
zeroDayNote: A scheduled job finds the newest 0-Day Week of … pack on your Torznab indexers, downloads it, and imports the missing issues of series already in your collection. Turn the schedule on from the Jobs page.
cloudflareNote: This site is behind Cloudflare, so it uses the FlareSolverr URL from Settings → Downloading.
cloudflareNoteBrowser: This site is behind Cloudflare, so it uses the FlareSolverr URL from Settings → Downloading; on the browser build it can also fall back to the built-in browser.
prioritySub: When more than one source can serve an issue, they're tried top-to-bottom — the first with a match wins.
metaSub: Where series and issue data comes from.
metaSourcesNote: Turn on every source you want series and issue data from. Searches ask all of them and show the answers together, best first, so the order decides which wins when two know the same series. A series keeps coming from the source that found it. The built-in service works out of the box; the others query a database directly with your own key or account, under its limits.
registered: Registered with the metadata service (instance key ends in {key}).
notRegistered: Not registered yet — this install provisions its key automatically on first use.
tagNote: Embedded writes ComicInfo.xml straight into the CBZ (.cbr downloads are converted to .cbz so they can be tagged). Sidecar writes the same metadata to a .xml file next to the archive and never modifies it — keeping files byte-identical for seeding and file-share hashing, and letting .cbr files stay .cbr. Each library can override this in its settings.
enrichLabel: Enrich metadata (characters, story arcs, ratings, issue extras)
enrichNote: When the metadata source supports it, adds enrichment on top of the base record: characters, teams and story arcs — which the base record has for only a small share of issues, and almost none published before 1980 — plus per-role credits, content ratings, series status and end year, price, UPC and story titles. Characters and arcs are written into ComicInfo.xml, so turning this off leaves those fields out of your files. A source without enrichment ignores the request, so it's safe either way.
mangaNote: How far manga search reaches into the manga catalogue's content ratings — each level includes the ones below it. Applies to the Add dialog's manga lane and manga-library imports.
releaseNote: The release provider feeds "This week's releases".
signinSub: How people sign in. Password login always works for admins.
signinNote: Add an SSO provider (e.g. OIDC) or another login backend from the Plugins page to let users sign in with an identity provider.
disablePasswordLogin: Disable password login (SSO only — admins keep a password fallback)
notifSub: Where BackIssue sends alerts. The in-app bell always records everything regardless. Open a channel to configure it.
noChannelsNote: Add the Notifications Hub plugin to send alerts to Discord, Telegram, Pushover, ntfy, or any webhook.
libMetaTitle: Where this library's series and issue data comes from
libMetaNote: This library's series are looked up through the sources ticked here, in this order. Turn them all off to go back to the default list.
metaDefaultForLibraries: This list is the default; a library can choose its own under Settings → Library.
saveNeedsLoad: Settings didn’t load — retry before saving.
